Subject: Draft MAP: data traceability & retention requirements (post-demo follow-up)

Hi Susan / Marco,

Thanks again for taking the demo yesterday — great discussion on the throughput and how you expect to route PHI-containing clinical summaries into inference flows. Per our ask, attached is a first-pass MAP focused on the data handling milestone we discussed. I pulled the sections we think need explicit acceptance criteria so we can get this checkpoint closed quickly.

Quick recap of the milestone we put in the MAP:
- Milestone name: Data traceability and retention acceptance
- Target owner: WellCare Security (customer) + Redwood compliance lead
- Target close date: 2027-05-10 (proposed)
- Success criteria: 
  - Retention policy documented (max retention windows per data class)
  - Audit trail demonstrating per-request logs for 90 days with per-token metadata
  - Data deletion workflow tested for sample dataset (10 records)
  - PHI handling: redaction and encryption requirements noted and validated

Open questions for you (to confirm in the MAP):
1) Which categories do you consider PHI vs. PII vs. general metadata for this workload?
2) Do you require field-level immutability logs or is request-level metadata sufficient?
3) Are there regulator-driven retention windows we must encode into the policy (e.g., state or payer-specific)?

Attachments: redwood-map-draft-v1.pdf (MAP sections highlighted), example-audit-trace.txt (sample log format we propose).

Next steps I propose:
- You send back the PHI/PII categorization by 2027-04-22
- We convert the MAP into a formal SOW appendix once categories are confirmed
- Marissa will schedule a 30-min call with our compliance engineer to walk through the audit trace format

If that timeline looks reasonable I’ll update the MAP and mark the milestone owners.

Thanks,
Sofia

Sofia — thanks for the clear summary and the MAP draft. A couple of clarifications from our side so we can sign off on the milestone: 

PHI/PII classification:
- PHI: any clinical note content, diagnosis codes, medication lists, lab results tied to an MRN or patient identifier.
- PII: name, email, phone, postal address.
- Metadata: request timestamp, calling service, tenant id — these are non-PHI but some IDs are considered sensitive.

Retention / audit asks:
- We need a 7 year retention policy for records with PHI for clinical review (state requirement).
- Audit trails must be queryable by request id and show: timestamp, model version, input hash, output hashes, redaction flag, and which key-encryption key was used (KMS id).
- For privacy, we prefer request-level metadata rather than storing full request text in logs. Can you confirm the example-audit-trace.txt can be configured to store hashes instead of raw inputs?

Certs & evidence:
- Please include a SOC 2 summary and the list of encryption-at-rest controls. We’ll need those for our security review.

Timing:
- We can confirm classifications by 2027-04-22 as requested. The 7-year retention makes the target close date of 2027-05-10 tight; is there a way to stage acceptance (e.g., sign off on logs + KMS integration first, then finalize retention language)?

Thanks — happy to discuss with your compliance engineer.

Best,
Susan
Dr. Susan Patel
Chief Privacy Officer | WellCare Health

Susan — great points, thank you. Looping Karthik (security) and Monica (compliance) to confirm technical feasibility and propose a split acceptance approach. Quick responses to your bullets: 

- Hashes vs raw inputs: yes, Redwood can log input/output hashes and a redaction flag instead of raw text. The example-audit-trace.txt shows a JSON-LD line format with hashes; we can swap raw_input for input_hash and still preserve per-request traceability.

- Audit trail fields: the set you listed (timestamp, model_version, input_hash, output_hash, redaction_flag, kms_key_id) is supported today. We will include model-commit and quantization profile fields in the trace as well.

- KMS evidence & SOC 2: attaching our SOC 2 summary. For KMS integration we support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own) or Redwood-managed with dedicated KMS keys per tenant.

- Proposed staging for acceptance: 
  1) Phase 1 (by 2027-05-10): Audit trail format & KMS integration validated, per-request hashes enabled, sample deletion tested on non-PHI dataset.
  2) Phase 2 (by 2027-06-15): Finalized retention windows encoded in the SOW appendix (7-year PHI retention), and full runbook approved.

Action items: 
- Karthik: please confirm the log retention tooling and whether we can provide query/export for customer audit (pinged below).
- Monica: please confirm the deletion workflow test plan and what evidence we can provide (screenshots, runbook steps).
- Sofia: can you confirm the staged dates with the customer once Karthik/Monica confirm?

Thanks all — quick technical confirmations from security: 

- Audit trace: we support storing only hashes for inputs/outputs. The trace will include: request_id, timestamp (ISO8601), model_version, input_hash (SHA256), output_hash (SHA256), redaction_flag (boolean), kms_key_id, tenant_id, and optional quantization_profile. That matches what Susan requested.

- Retention windows: our platform supports configurable retention policies per-tenant and per-data-class. For PHI we can mark logs as "long-retention" and attach lifecycle rules (7 years). We'll include an exportable index that allows WellCare to run on-demand queries for audit. Exports are available as encrypted CSVs with access logs.

- Deletion workflow: we can run a verified deletion test using a nonce dataset. Monica will own the test and provide signed attestations plus logs showing deletion confirmations.

- Dependencies: customer-managed KMS requires SX-approval on KMS access; if you choose Redwood-managed KMS we can stand up dedicated keys by 2027-05-05.

I can join a 30-min technical sync this week — propose 2027-04-21 10:00am PT.

Karthik
Head of Security Engineering | Redwood Inference
